# Choosing the deployment topology, and who runs migrations

The `rimsky` image's entrypoint reads its command argument. No command runs all
three roles in one process; a single role name runs that role alone. Migrations
run exactly once per deployment whatever the split.

## The four legal launches

```bash
# all three roles in one process
docker run -d -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" rimsky:<tag>

# one role each
docker run -d -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" rimsky:<tag> rimsky-control-api
docker run -d -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" rimsky:<tag> rimsky-scheduler
docker run -d -v "$PWD/rimsky.yml:/etc/rimsky/rimsky.yml:ro" rimsky:<tag> rimsky-supervisor
```

The no-command container reports all three roles and runs them in a single
process. A `rimsky-control-api` container runs that role alone — its process
table holds the entrypoint and one control-api child — and answers on the
control API.

## Illegal launches fail immediately

```bash
docker run rimsky:<tag> rimsky-nonsense              # exit 2
docker run rimsky:<tag> rimsky-migrate               # exit 2
docker run rimsky:<tag> rimsky-scheduler rimsky-supervisor   # exit 2
```

An unknown role name and `rimsky-migrate` are both refused as unknown roles,
naming the three valid ones. Two role arguments are refused for exceeding one.
Nothing starts. A mistyped choice fails at once rather than producing a
half-formed deployment.

## Migrations run once across a split

Run scheduler, supervisor and control-api against one database. Exactly one
container runs the migrations — the control-api one — and the other two log that
they are skipping them. The schema arrives, the deployment serves, and a node
dispatches and settles at `terminal/success` across the split roles.

Give each role a restart policy, so a role that starts before the schema exists
retries.

## Moving migration ownership

`RIMSKY_ENTRYPOINT_MIGRATE` overrides the default in both directions.

```bash
# a no-command container that would otherwise own the migrations skips them
docker run -d -e RIMSKY_ENTRYPOINT_MIGRATE=0 ... rimsky:<tag>

# a scheduler-only container that would otherwise skip runs them
docker run -d -e RIMSKY_ENTRYPOINT_MIGRATE=1 ... rimsky:<tag> rimsky-scheduler
```

That second form is what a dedicated one-shot init step needs.

Any other value fails startup:

```bash
docker run -e RIMSKY_ENTRYPOINT_MIGRATE=yes ... rimsky:<tag>
# exit 2, naming the variable, the value it was given, and the two legal values
```

A typo cannot quietly change who migrates.
